A printed game card, sheet, or group of tickets may include several separate tickets, which can be divided from one another by perforations, score lines, folds, or similar features. In some embodiments, each individual ticket on the card or sheet is printed with at least one playable game. These games may be instant-win games that include game indicia covered by one or more removable layers, such as varnish or a rubber-based coating, which can be removed to expose the indicia.

Each ticket within the game card, sheet, or ticket set may also carry its own validation and/or activation markings. These markings may be readable by a person, by a computer, or by both. In addition, the complete game card, sheet, or ticket set may include activation indicia for the game or sheet as a whole, allowing all of the individual game tickets on the sheet to be activated at the same time when the full sheet is sold. When the validation codes for the individual game tickets are scanned or otherwise read, embodiments of the invention can determine separately whether each ticket is a winning ticket and whether that ticket has already been redeemed.
outputs.L3:
A printed game card, sheet, or ticket set may be configured to include multiple individual tickets formed as part of a single physical article. The individual tickets may be separated from one another by perforations, scoring, fold lines, weakened tear lines, cut lines, or other separation features that allow each ticket to be detached or otherwise distinguished from the remainder of the card, sheet, or set.

Each individual ticket may include at least one playable instant-win game. For example, a ticket may include one or more play areas covered by removable covering layers, such as scratch-off coatings or other opaque or concealing materials. When the removable covering layer is removed by a player, underlying game indicia are revealed. These game indicia may determine or indicate whether the ticket is a winning ticket, the prize amount or prize type, or other game-related information.

Each individual ticket may also include its own validation indicia, activation indicia, or both. Such indicia may be human-readable, computer-readable, or a combination of both. Human-readable indicia may include numbers, letters, symbols, or printed codes that can be read by a person. Computer-readable indicia may include barcodes, QR codes, magnetic codes, optical codes, RFID elements, or other machine-readable identifiers. These indicia can be used to identify the particular ticket, validate gameplay results, confirm eligibility for redemption, or support tracking and inventory control.

In addition to the indicia provided on each individual ticket, the overall game card, sheet, or ticket set may include separate activation indicia associated with the entire set. This activation indicia may allow all of the individual tickets included in the card, sheet, or set to be activated at the same time, such as when the set is sold at a retail location. For example, a retailer or point-of-sale system may scan or otherwise read a single activation code on the set, thereby activating each ticket contained within that set without requiring each individual ticket to be scanned separately.

When a player presents an individual ticket for validation or redemption, the validation indicia associated with that ticket may be read by a validation system. The system can use the validation code to determine whether the ticket corresponds to a winning outcome and, if so, the applicable prize. The system can also determine whether the ticket has already been redeemed, thereby helping to prevent duplicate redemption, fraud, or unauthorized claims. In this manner, the printed card, sheet, or ticket set can provide convenient multi-ticket sales and activation while still enabling each individual ticket to be independently played, validated, and redeemed.
outputs.L4:
A printed game card, sheet, or ticket set is provided that includes a plurality of separable instant-win tickets formed together on a common substrate. The tickets may be arranged in rows, columns, panels, strips, or any other convenient layout, and may be divided from one another by perforations, score lines, tear lines, cut lines, or other separation features that allow individual tickets to be removed from the sheet after purchase or distribution.

Each individual ticket includes its own game play area containing game indicia. The game indicia may be concealed by a removable covering, such as a scratch-off coating, pull-tab layer, peel-off label, or other obscuring material. When the covering is removed, the player can view the game indicia to determine whether that particular ticket is a winning ticket according to the rules of the game. The game indicia may include symbols, numbers, words, prize amounts, matching elements, or any other information used to indicate the outcome of the game.

In addition to the game indicia, each ticket includes an individual validation code, activation code, serial number, barcode, QR code, magnetic stripe, RFID element, or other machine-readable or human-readable identifier. This identifier is unique to the ticket or otherwise associated with that ticket in a validation database. The identifier allows a retailer, terminal, mobile device, server, or redemption system to determine whether the ticket is valid, whether it has been activated, whether it is a winning ticket, and whether any prize associated with the ticket has already been redeemed.

The sheet may also include sheet-level activation indicia. The sheet-level indicia may be printed on a border, header, detachable panel, cover portion, receipt portion, or other area of the sheet. This sheet-level indicia may represent the entire group of tickets on the sheet, or a defined subset of tickets on the sheet. For example, a single barcode or activation number may be scanned at the point of sale to activate all tickets included on the sheet in one transaction. This allows a retailer to sell a complete sheet, card, or packet of tickets without having to scan or activate each ticket separately.

When the sheet is sold, the retailer or sales terminal may read the sheet-level activation indicia and transmit the corresponding information to a central activation or validation system. The system then marks all tickets associated with that sheet as active. Once activated, the individual tickets may be separated from the sheet and distributed to different players, retained by a single purchaser, or otherwise used independently. Each ticket remains individually identifiable and may be validated separately using its own ticket-level code.

This arrangement provides both bulk activation and individual validation. Bulk activation improves speed and convenience at the point of sale because a group of tickets can be activated simultaneously. At the same time, individual ticket validation maintains security and accountability because each ticket can still be checked separately for winning status, authenticity, activation state, and prior redemption. If a player presents a ticket for prize payment, the validation system can determine whether that specific ticket was part of an activated sheet, whether the ticket contains a winning outcome, and whether the prize has already been claimed.

The system is useful for instant-win lottery tickets, promotional game pieces, raffle-style tickets, sweepstakes entries, charity gaming products, amusement tickets, or other printed game articles. It allows multiple instant-win tickets to be manufactured and sold as a unit while preserving the ability to track, validate, and redeem each ticket individually. This reduces handling time, supports efficient sales of ticket sheets or bundles, and helps prevent unauthorized use, duplicate redemption, and payment of prizes on tickets that were not properly activated.

Each ticket portion includes game play indicia concealed by a removable scratch-off coating and one or more ticket-level validation or activation indicia, including machine-readable or human-readable codes, numbers, symbols, or encoded data. The sheet further includes sheet-level validation or activation indicia associated with the plurality of ticket portions collectively, the sheet-level indicia being distinct from or correlated with the ticket-level indicia to permit activation, inventory control, sale verification, redemption verification, or deactivation of the entire sheet and/or selected ticket portions. counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a technical summary of an invention for a game card or ticket set where each ticket has separate validation codes, but the entire sheet can be activated at once when sold.
counterfactuals.output:
## Technical Summary

The invention relates to a game card, lottery ticket, promotional ticket, or similar wagering/entertainment article provided as a multi-ticket set, sheet, strip, booklet, or pack. Each individual ticket within the set includes its own separate validation code for prize redemption or game verification, while the set as a whole includes a common activation feature that permits all tickets in the set to be activated in a single transaction at the point of sale.

In one embodiment, a sheet includes a plurality of separable tickets joined by perforations or other weakened separation lines. Each ticket bears unique game indicia and a unique validation code, such as a barcode, QR code, alphanumeric code, encrypted code, or machine-readable symbol. The validation code may be concealed under a scratch-off coating, printed in a secure area, or otherwise protected against unauthorized viewing prior to play or redemption.

The sheet further includes a sheet-level activation code, such as a master barcode or serial number, printed on a margin, header, backing, cover, package, or other common portion of the ticket set. The sheet-level activation code is associated in a central database with the individual validation codes of all tickets included in that sheet. When the sheet is sold, a retailer or terminal scans or enters the sheet-level activation code. In response, a validation server or lottery/game management system changes the status of each associated individual ticket from an inactive, unsold, or non-redeemable state to an active, sold, or redeemable state.

This arrangement allows a retailer to activate an entire multi-ticket sheet with a single scan rather than scanning each ticket separately, reducing transaction time and minimizing errors. At the same time, each ticket remains independently playable and independently redeemable because each ticket retains its own unique validation code. Upon redemption, a player or retailer submits the individual ticket validation code to the system, which verifies that the ticket belongs to an activated sheet, determines the ticket’s prize or play outcome, and updates the ticket status to redeemed, paid, void, or otherwise processed.

The system may include safeguards to prevent redemption of tickets from sheets that have not been activated, to detect duplicate redemption attempts, and to track sales and inventory at the sheet and ticket levels. The database may store relationships among sheet identifiers, individual ticket identifiers, activation status, retailer information, sale time, prize status, and redemption history. The activation code may be physically separated from the individual tickets, printed in a non-play area, or provided on packaging to prevent customer access prior to sale.

The invention is useful for instant lottery tickets, pull-tab games, raffle sheets, promotional game cards, amusement tickets, sweepstakes entries, collectible game cards with prize features, or other ticket-based games where multiple tickets are manufactured and sold as a unit but must be validated individually. The invention improves retail efficiency while maintaining ticket-level security, accounting, and prize validation.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: In formal patent language, describe embodiments of a printed instant game ticket sheet incorporating perforations, scratch-off indicia, human-readable/computer-readable codes, and redemption tracking.
counterfactuals.output:
In one embodiment, a printed instant game ticket sheet comprises a substrate having a first surface and an opposed second surface, the substrate being formed from paperboard, cardstock, polymeric film, laminated stock, or another printable sheet material suitable for use in lottery, promotional, charitable gaming, sweepstakes, or other instant-win applications. The substrate may define a plurality of discrete ticket regions arranged in rows, columns, arrays, strips, panels, or other predetermined layouts. Adjacent ticket regions may be separated, at least in part, by one or more lines of weakness, such as perforations, micro-perforations, score lines, die-cut lines, kiss-cut lines, tear lines, or combinations thereof, thereby permitting individual tickets to be detached from the sheet while maintaining the integrity of the remaining tickets prior to detachment.

In certain embodiments, each ticket region includes a game play area bearing one or more printed indicia. The printed indicia may include variable game indicia, fixed instructional indicia, prize indicia, authentication indicia, validation indicia, security indicia, branding indicia, advertising indicia, or combinations thereof. At least a portion of the game indicia may be concealed by a removable opaque coating, such as a scratch-off coating, latex coating, foil layer, overprint layer, or other removable masking material. The removable coating may be applied over selected indicia so that a purchaser or player may remove the coating to reveal concealed information, including symbols, numbers, letters, images, prize values, winning or losing outcomes, multipliers, bonus designations, or other game outcome information.

In some embodiments, the ticket sheet further comprises one or more human-readable codes and one or more computer-readable codes associated with each ticket region, with the sheet as a whole, or both. The human-readable code may comprise an alphanumeric serial number, ticket number, pack number, sheet number, batch number, game number, retailer number, validation number, redemption code, prize code, or other visible identifier. The computer-readable code may comprise a linear barcode, two-dimensional barcode, QR code, Data Matrix code, PDF417 code, optical character recognition code, magnetic code, RFID element, NFC element, or other machine-readable identifier. The human-readable code and the computer-readable code may encode the same information, partially overlapping information, or different information. In certain embodiments, the computer-readable code encodes a unique ticket identifier corresponding to a record maintained in a ticket management database.

In one embodiment, the printed instant game ticket sheet comprises a master sheet identifier associated with the sheet and a plurality of individual ticket identifiers associated respectively with the plurality of ticket regions. The master sheet identifier may be printed in human-readable form, computer-readable form, or both. Each individual ticket identifier may be unique within a game, within a batch, within a print run, within a retailer allocation, or within an entire redemption system. In some embodiments, the individual ticket identifier is logically associated with a predetermined game outcome stored in a secure data file or generated and printed during production.

In certain embodiments, each ticket region includes a redemption area. The redemption area may include a validation code, claim code, redemption barcode, prize verification number, concealed validation indicia, or other information used to verify eligibility for redemption. The redemption area may be visible, concealed beneath a scratch-off coating, partially concealed, or otherwise protected from premature access. In one implementation, the redemption code is different from the game play indicia revealed by the player, thereby providing an independent validation mechanism. In another implementation, the redemption code is correlated with the displayed game result to confirm that the ticket is valid and that the displayed result corresponds to an authorized outcome.

In further embodiments, the printed instant game ticket sheet is configured for redemption tracking. A redemption tracking system may comprise a computing device, server, point-of-sale terminal, mobile device, scanner, network interface, and database configured to receive ticket identifier information from the human-readable or computer-readable code. Upon presentation of a ticket for redemption, a scanner or user input device may capture the ticket identifier, validation code, or both, and transmit the captured information to the redemption tracking system. The system may compare the captured information against stored ticket records to determine whether the ticket is authentic, whether the ticket corresponds to a winning outcome, whether the ticket has previously been redeemed, whether the ticket is associated with an active game, whether the ticket is assigned to an authorized retailer or distribution channel, and whether the ticket satisfies one or more redemption rules.

In some embodiments, the redemption tracking system updates a ticket status field in response to a redemption event. The ticket status field may include values such as unissued, issued, activated, sold, unsold, redeemed, void, expired, stolen, cancelled, claimed, pending verification, or paid. The system may record redemption data including a redemption timestamp, redemption location, retailer identifier, terminal identifier, operator identifier, claimant information, prize amount, payment method, audit log entry, geolocation data, or other tracking information. The system may prevent duplicate redemption by rejecting subsequent redemption attempts for a ticket identifier previously recorded as redeemed, claimed, void, expired, or otherwise ineligible.

In one embodiment, the ticket sheet is produced using a printing process in which variable data corresponding to game outcomes and ticket identifiers is printed on the substrate, followed by application of one or more protective or concealing layers over selected areas. The printing process may include offset printing, digital printing, inkjet printing, laser printing, flexographic printing, gravure printing, thermal transfer printing, screen printing, or combinations thereof. Security features may be incorporated into the substrate, inks, coatings, or printed indicia, including ultraviolet-responsive inks, infrared-responsive inks, microprinting, guilloche patterns, void pantographs, chemical alteration indicators, tamper-evident coatings, holographic elements, serialized numbering, encrypted codes, check digits, cryptographic signatures, or forensic markers.

In certain embodiments, the perforations are arranged to define detachable ticket portions while preserving one or more retained portions of the sheet. For example, the ticket sheet may include a stub, header, control strip, accounting strip, or retailer-retained portion separated from one or more player-retained ticket portions by perforation lines. The retained portion may bear duplicate or related ticket identifiers, pack identifiers, batch identifiers, or inventory control codes to facilitate accounting, activation, reconciliation, distribution tracking, or audit functions. In some embodiments, removal of an individual ticket from the sheet exposes, separates, or preserves corresponding tracking information on the retained portion.

In another embodiment, each ticket region comprises a first code accessible before play and a second code accessible after removal of the scratch-off coating. The first code may be used for inventory activation, sale tracking, or preliminary authentication, while the second code may be used for prize validation or final redemption. The second code may be concealed to reduce unauthorized validation attempts before purchase or play. The redemption tracking system may require both the first code and the second code, or a derived value based on both codes, to authorize payment of a prize.

In some embodiments, the game ticket sheet includes a plurality of detachable tickets having respective outcome indicia concealed beneath scratch-off coatings and respective redemption codes printed in association therewith, wherein the redemption codes are uniquely mapped to a prize table maintained by a central server. The central server may store, for each ticket identifier, at least one of a game number, pack number, sheet number, ticket position, prize value, expected outcome, activation status, sale status, redemption status, expiration date, retailer assignment, and validation hash. When a redemption request is received, the server may determine whether the received code corresponds to a valid unredeemed winning ticket and may return an authorization, denial, prize amount, or instruction for manual review.

In further embodiments, the ticket sheet may include alignment marks, registration marks, cut marks, sequence marks, or production control marks for verifying proper placement of perforations, printed indicia, scratch-off coatings, and codes. The scratch-off coating may be positioned in registration with concealed indicia and may comprise one or more layers, including a release layer, opacity layer, color layer, security layer, and printable overcoat. The overcoat may bear instructions such as “scratch here,” graphic icons, play symbols, or other visible matter that does not reveal the concealed outcome prior to removal.

In one exemplary embodiment, a printed instant game ticket sheet comprises: a substrate; a plurality of ticket portions defined on the substrate; a plurality of perforation lines separating adjacent ticket portions; for each ticket portion, a concealed game play field comprising prize-determining indicia covered by a removable scratch-off coating; for each ticket portion, a visible human-readable identifier; for each ticket portion, a computer-readable identifier encoding at least a portion of the visible identifier or a related validation identifier; and a redemption tracking association between the computer-readable identifier and a database record representing a redemption state of the corresponding ticket portion. The redemption state is changeable from an unredeemed state to a redeemed state upon successful validation of the ticket portion, thereby inhibiting repeated redemption of the same ticket portion.

In another exemplary embodiment, a method of manufacturing a printed instant game ticket sheet comprises generating a plurality of ticket records, each ticket record including a unique identifier, game outcome data, and redemption status data; printing, on a substrate, a plurality of ticket regions corresponding to the plurality of ticket records; printing concealed game indicia and at least one visible or scannable code for each ticket region; applying a removable scratch-off coating over at least a portion of the concealed game indicia; forming perforations between adjacent ticket regions; and storing or updating the plurality of ticket records in a redemption tracking database. The method may further comprise verifying correspondence between printed codes and stored ticket records, activating a sheet or pack of tickets, recording sale data, and updating redemption status upon presentation of a ticket for prize claim.

In still another embodiment, a method of redeeming a printed instant game ticket comprises receiving, by a redemption terminal, a computer-readable code from a ticket detached from a perforated ticket sheet; transmitting ticket identifier data derived from the code to a redemption server; retrieving a stored record corresponding to the ticket identifier data; determining, based on the stored record, whether the ticket is authentic, active, unexpired, unredeemed, and associated with a winning outcome; authorizing redemption when the determining step indicates that the ticket is eligible; and updating the stored record to indicate that the ticket has been redeemed. The method may further comprise storing audit information and preventing subsequent redemption attempts associated with the same ticket identifier.

The foregoing embodiments may be implemented individually or in any suitable combination. Features described with respect to one embodiment may be incorporated into another embodiment without departing from the scope of the disclosed printed instant game ticket sheet, manufacturing methods, and redemption tracking systems.
